title: Why India Is a Key Emerging Market for the Estée Lauder Cos. | United States
text:
The Estée Lauder Cos. considers India to be a catalyst market.
Cosmetics was launched, followed by Estée Lauder and Clinique. Today, the group has 14 brands in India and ranks first in prestige skin care and prestige makeup.
The fragrance business is on the rise.
“The Estée Lauder Companies has been an early mover and a builder of prestige beauty in the Indian market,” said Nadine Graf, president, Europe, Middle East and Africa; U.K. and Ireland, and emerging markets, highlighting the group’s partnerships with retailers such as Nykaa. “Online has been a game changer and continues to be a big, big growth-driver. ”Icons Only: How the Estée Lauder Cos.
Built Its Billion-dollar Brand Club In addition to marketing its own brands in India, the company is investing in the market as well. In 2008, Lauder made a minority investment in the Ayurvedic beauty brand Forest Essentials, then increased its ownership stake in 2020. Earlier this year, it acquired the remaining shares to take full ownership.
“We see a tremendous potential of acceleration in India,” said Estée Lauder Cos. chief executive officer Stéphane de La Faverie. “I believe after K-beauty Indian beauty is the next wave, and Forest Essentials has a massive role to play in accelerating this next wave. ” As with other emerging markets, a key opportunity for Lauder is to tap into the growing middle class as they trade up in their purchasing habits.
Whereas 90 percent of beauty sales come from the mass market, just 10 percent are generated by prestige products.
“So imagine the opportunity with regards to sourcing and recruiting from mass,” Graf said. “That’s just immense. ” The cadre of working women also present a major opportunity. But that doesn’t mean it’s a one-size-fits-all proposition.
“How are we going differently to market? ” Graf said.
“We need different shades, different formulas, different claims that are very relevant for that particular country. ” Lauder delves into local consumer insights through domestic focus groups and culls data from its own stores and partners’ stores to understand key concerns and the beauty habits of a country’s consumer, such as the disproportionate use of kajal in India. Lauder produces products from different brands specifically for the Indian consumer, which don’t necessarily stay in India but instead travel globally.
The group also recruits new customers through smaller sizes. Some of Lauder’s most iconic products, such as Estée Lauder’s Advanced Night Repair, come in a 7-ml. bottle. TheFix+ spray is also offered in a small, 13-ml. size.
“If we are saying we need to source consumers from mass, it means you need to make luxury and prestige more accessible,” Graf said. A brand like The Ordinary, with lower price points, is well placed to source consumers into mass/masstige, then trade up.
“Also MAC…is positioned to build that bridge from mass into prestige, and so are different brands in different price tiers,” Graf said. “Across emerging markets we talk about more than 1 billion Gen Z consumers, and they are all digital-savvy, which means the opportunity of continuous growth and really establishing fragrances is something that we make an absolute top priority,” Graf said.
Last but certainly not least, there’s the focus on communicating local relevancy as a differentiator without weakening brand equity and DNA. The Estée Lauder Cos. creates campaigns around religious holidays or other important cultural moments, such as Diwali, Ramadan or bridal in India, where the wedding season is significant.
“That’s consumer-centricity — to understand what matters to her,” Graf said. “How do you make sure you’re relevant in the context of the local ways of doing things? ” To wit: MAC recently launched a bridal campaign, called “Forever in MAC,” specifically for the Indian market. It takes the traditional, local idea of the family wedding portrait bringing various generations together, but through the lens of the brand and its global DNA.
Graf described this as “artistry, individuality, self-expression. ” “That’s a completely different level of going to market, and the way Beauty Reimagined is coming to life,” Graf said, referring to de La Faverie’s go-to-market strategy.
“Desirability is built globally, but the relevance is built locally. And it takes both to win the consumer nowadays. ” Other examples are Kilian Paris campaigns for Eid and Ramadan in the Middle East, and the Jo Malone campaign for the festive season of Diwali in Southeast Asia.
“You would immediately recognize the brand DNA, which is very global, but in a setting that is very locally relevant,” Graf said. “And that’s a game-changer in the way that we are reaching that consumer. ” In all geographies Lauder remains on the lookout for possible brand acquisitions to fill portfolio white spaces, as with Forest Essentials.
“When we look at the intersection on where Forest Essentials sits globally speaking, it’s very interesting,” Graf said. “It’s the number-one prestige skin care brand in India that has the potential to travel globally. ” From Forest Essentials, Lauder has gleaned many local consumer insights — including how women shop and what they care about.
“It’s a beautiful story,” Graf said. “And we are very happy to take it to the next level now. ”WWD and Women's Wear Daily are part of PMX Global, LLC, a subsidiary of Penske Media Corporation. © 2026 Fairchild Publishing, LLC. All rights reserved.
